findings.summary: The note promises hash-based names for every non-default branch, but the router also falls back to counter names when it cannot read branch identity. Those worktrees can still produce shared names.
evidence: The note says “On any branch other than `main`, `master`, `trunk`, or `develop`” the record includes a branch hash.
`_head_branch` returns `None` when it cannot read or parse the `.git` link or `HEAD`; `resolved_followup_record_payload` then uses the shared `followup` counter sequence.
findings.action: Scope the hash guarantee to non-default branches whose identity the router can read, and state that unreadable branch metadata also uses the counter.

counterweight_triage.disposition: The note now limits the claim to non-default branches and states that default branches and detached HEADs retain the counter. The unreadable-branch-metadata fallback remains unmentioned.

next_move: Add the readable-branch-identity condition and mention the counter fallback when branch metadata cannot be read.
non_claims: Reviewed the six identity-bound inline semantic inputs; did not inspect workspace paths or run tests.
The hashed naming guarantee remains subject to 8-hex hash-prefix collisions.
